headline: Held public hearing on $146,617.94 transfer into opioid abatement trust fund.
summary: Director Bobbie Bagley said the money would pay for housing help, sober living support, grants to partner groups, and the winter warming station. Resident Laura Colquhoun opposed using the fund for warming station costs and staff salaries, and asked that those costs be paid from the general fund. No one spoke in favor.
plain_text:
A special meeting of the Board of Aldermen was held Monday, November 23, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. in the aldermanic 
chamber and duly noticed in two places, including the City’s website, in accordance with the requirements of RSA 91-
A:2 II. 
 
President Lori Wilshire presided; Alderman-at-Large Michael B. O’Brien, Sr. recorded. 
 
Prayer was offered by Alderman-at-Large Michael B. O’Brien, Sr.; Alderman Richard A. Dowd led in the Pledge to the 
Flag. 
 
Let’s start the meeting by taking a roll call attendance.   
 
Alderman-at-Large Michael B. O’Brien, Sr. called the roll. 
 
The roll call was taken with 12 members of the Board of Aldermen present:  Alderman Klee, Alderwoman Smith, 
Alderman Thibeault, Alderman O’Brien, Alderman Gregg (via Zoom), Alderman Dowd, Alderman Sullivan, Alderman 
Sennott, Alderman Johnson, Alderwoman Kelly, Alderman Morgan, President Wilshire.       
 
Alderman Clemons, Alderman Ravan, and Alderman Lopez, were recorded absent. 
 
President Wilshire 
 
I’m going to turn the meeting over to the Chair of the Budget Review Committee – Alderman Dowd. 
 
Chairman Dowd 
 
Yes, this evening we have a public hearing on R-26-077 Relative to the Supplemental Appropriation of $146,617.94 of 
FY2027 Unanticipated Revenue into Fund #7024 “Opioid Abatement Expendable Trust Fund” .  Is there someone here 
that would like to explain the. 
 
PUBLIC HEARING 
 
R-26-077 
RELATIVE TO THE SUPPLEMENTAL APPROPRIATION OF $146,617.94 OF FY2027 UNANTICIPATED 
REVENUE INTO FUND #7024 “OPIOID ABATEMENT EXPENDABLE TRUST FUND” 
 
Bobbie Bagley, Division of Public Health and Community Services Director 
 
Good evening and thank you.  Bobbie Bagley, Director of Division of Public Health and Community Services.  Here to 
speak on R-26-077.  So the appropriation of this $146,617.94 will support the efforts that we have for the opioid 
abatement response that we have here in the City of Nashua.  Apparently right now, we have a closing balance of 
$291,506.30.  The funds that go into this account are used to support assistance that we provide for individuals in the 
community that have passed this year of opioid abatement use, or current history of opioid use that we provide 
shelter/support for them.  Meaning that if they need assistance with housing, we will support that.   
 
We also help support sober living housing, which is really, really important for individuals who are in recovery.  
Without housing, we have found that individuals will not sustain their recovery efforts at all.  We also are providing 
other public service activities, which includes granting out to some of our partners that are doing opioid abatement 
work.  So this funds that we’re receiving will add into this cash of funds so that we can continue that work.   
 
We also support our winter warming station.  The per diem staff that works there as well as all of the supp lies that are 
needed come out of the opioid abatement fund and it also supports any other services that we provide.  For instance, 
the mental health services that we provide or any other service providers that work with us. 
 
We currently just opened up the warming station, so we will start occurring more funds against this account and we 
just granted two organizations funding for applications they submitted to us.  So it is really important for us to have this 
money appropriated into this account.  We do expect that over the next – we still have about 14 more years that the 
opioid abatement funds will be coming into the City of Nashua and it’s usually under the unanticipated revenue 
because it can’t predict what the amount of these checks will be when they come in.   
 
Chairman Dowd
Special Board of Aldermen                                          08-24-2026                        Page 2 
 
Any clarifying questions? 
 
Alderman Thibeault 
 
Thank you Mr. Chair.  And this can only be used for the opioid abatement because it comes from the lawsuit, correct? 
 
Bobbie Bagley, Division of Public Health and Community Services Director 
 
That is correct.   
 
Alderman Thibeault 
 
Okay.  Thank you. 
 
Chairman Dowd 
 
Any other amplifying questions?  Seeing none.  Thank you Director Bagley.   
 
Bobbie Bagley, Division of Public Health and Community Services Director 
 
Thank you. 
 
Testimony in Favor - None 
 
Testimony in Opposition 
 
Laura Colquhoun 
 
Laura Colquhoun at 33 Greenwood Drive.  I was and I think most Nashua residents feel that the primary purpose of 
the city’s Opioid Abatement Expendable Trust Fund was to receive, hold, and spend money obtained from the opioid 
liquidation settlement exclusively on programs that addressed the harms caused by the addiction.  These funds are 
coming from lawsuits against the opioid manufacturers and distributors.   
 
RSA 126-A:86 requires funds to be used for the opioid abatement projects.  This means it was to reduce the impact of 
the opioid crisis through prevention programs, treatment centers, recovery support services, harm reduction 
incentatives, community education, and outreach programs that help individuals and family affected by the opioid 
addiction.   
 
Putting these funds in a expandable fund account segregates the money from the general fund.  It also ensures that 
the funds are spent only on legally authorized purpose.  As a matter of fact, Nashua saw overdoses hit a record low in 
2025.  However, these funds are currently being used for the warming station which is not only used by people who 
have drug problems but people who do not have a home.  These funds are paying for salaries of the community 
health workers.  This is not a legally obligated program that should be funded.  That should come out of directly out of 
the community health programs.   
 
In 2026, the city used 165 in additional funds; $51,000 in 2024; 120 in 2025; and now 147.  In order to be transparent, 
the city should only be charging costs directly related to drug use.  These expenses should come out of the 
Community Health budget and not be put in this opioid expendable trust fund.  The city is not being transparent with 
these expenses.  I asked this Budget Review Committee to do the right thing and assign these expenses to the 
general fund and not the Opioid Abatement Expendable Trust Fund  Thank you. 
 
Testimony in Favor - None 
 
Testimony in Opposition - None 
 
Chairman Dowd closed the public hearing on Resolution R-26-077 at 7:09 p.m. 
 
ADJOURNMENT 
 
MOTION BY ALDERMAN WILSHIRE THAT THE NOVEMBER 23, 2026 SPECIAL MEETING OF THE BOARD OF 
ALDERMEN BE ADJOURNED, BY ROLL CALL
Special Board of Aldermen                                          08-24-2026                        Page 3 
 
 
A viva voce roll call was taken, which resulted as follows: 
 
Yea: Alderman Klee, Alderwoman Smith, Alderman Thibeault, Alderman O’Brien,  
 Alderman Gregg, Alderman Dowd, Alderman Sullivan, Alderman Sennott,  
 Alderman Johnson, Alderwoman Kelly, Alderman Morgan, Alderman Wilshire    12      
 
Nay:                               0 
 
MOTION CARRIED 
 
The meeting was declared adjourned at 7:10 p.m.   
 
               Alderman-at-Large Michael B. O’Brien, Sr. 
               Clerk
